name: Holographic Renormalisation Group Flow
description: Walls of scalar field in anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions, dual to flows of the renormalisation group of $\mathcal{N} = 4$ super Yang-Mills theory, with the distance from the boundary as the energy scale. Luciano Girardello, Michela Petrini, Massimo Porrati, and Alberto Zaffaroni built them in 1998, and wherever the null energy condition holds a $c$-function falls along them toward the infrared.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Under Juan Maldacena's correspondence, two regions of anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions with different radii, joined by a wall of scalar field, correspond to two conformal field theories joined by a flow of the renormalisation group [maldacena1998, girardello1998, freedman1999]. The region near the boundary corresponds to the field theory at high energies and the region deep inside to its fixed point at low energies, and the cube of each radius sets the central charge at that end [girardello1998, freedman1999]. Luciano Girardello, Michela Petrini, Massimo Porrati, and Alberto Zaffaroni found such walls in October 1998 in the gauged supergravity of five dimensions, between the critical point of its potential dual to $\mathcal{N} = 4$ super Yang-Mills theory and two critical points with no supersymmetry [girardello1998]. They proved that the walls exist by treating the scalar as a particle that rolls, with friction that stays positive, from one critical point to the other, and they gave a function of the radius that equals the central charge at each end and decreases toward the infrared [girardello1998]. Jacques Distler and Frederic Zamora reached the same critical points a few days later and found the point with $SU(3)$ symmetry stable and the point with $SO(5)$ symmetry unstable [girardello1998, distler1998].¶Daniel Z. Freedman, Steven S. Gubser, Krzysztof Pilch, and Nicholas P. Warner wrote the most general metric with the symmetries of flat spacetime along the wall in April 1999, $ds^2 = e^{2A(r)}\eta_{\mu\nu}dx^\mu dx^\nu + dr^2$, with $r$ the proper distance across it and $A = r/L$ for anti-de Sitter space of radius $L$ [freedman1999]. Their wall keeps an eighth of the supersymmetry and "interpolates between an exterior anti-de Sitter region with maximal supersymmetry and an interior anti-de Sitter region with one quarter of the maximal supersymmetry" [freedman1999]. Its field theory is $\mathcal{N} = 4$ super Yang-Mills theory with a mass for one of its three adjoint chiral superfields, and the central charges at the two ends stand in the ratio $27/32$, the value computed in the field theory [freedman1999]. Demanding that the supersymmetry survive, Freedman and coauthors reduced the equations of motion to equations of first order, a gradient flow of a superpotential $W$ of the scalars with $A' = -gW/3$ for the gauge coupling $g$ of the supergravity [freedman1999]. They integrated the wall numerically, starting from the infrared end, where small errors decay [freedman1999]. From Einstein's equations they showed that $A'' \le 0$ for any such metric whose matter obeys the null energy condition, so that $\mathcal{C}(r) = \mathcal{C}_0/A'^3$, with $\mathcal{C}_0$ a constant, does not increase toward the infrared and equals the central charge wherever the geometry is anti-de Sitter [freedman1999].¶Kostas Skenderis and Paul K. Townsend found such equations of first order in 1999 for walls of a scalar whose potential admits a stable anti-de Sitter vacuum, with $e^{A}$ as the scale of the renormalisation group [skenderis1999]. Oliver DeWolfe, Freedman, Gubser, and Andreas Karch showed that the potential $V$ of a single scalar $\phi$ can be written as $V = \tfrac{1}{8}\left(\partial W/\partial\phi\right)^2 - \tfrac{1}{3}W^2$ by solving for $W$ [dewolfe2000]. Every flat wall of the scalar then solves $\phi' = \tfrac{1}{2}\partial W/\partial\phi$ and $A' = -W/3$ for some $W$, with or without supersymmetry [dewolfe2000]. With $W = 3/L - b\phi^2$, for a constant $b$, they solved these equations in closed form, and used the solution to fix the distance between the two walls of Lisa Randall and Raman Sundrum's construction, after Walter Goldberger and Mark Wise [dewolfe2000, randall1999a, goldberger1999]. DeWolfe and coauthors also suggested $|W|^{-3}$ as a $c$-function for flows without supersymmetry [dewolfe2000].¶Girardello, Petrini, Porrati, and Zaffaroni solved a supersymmetric flow in closed form, from $\mathcal{N} = 4$ super Yang-Mills theory with one mass for all three of its chiral superfields to pure $\mathcal{N} = 1$ super Yang-Mills theory [girardello2000]. Up to a constant factor, its warp factor is $e^{2A} = e^{2r/L} - 1$, with $r$ measured from a curvature singularity at $r = 0$, and it grows as $e^{2r/L}$ toward the boundary [girardello2000, bianchi2001]. Quarks confine and magnetic monopoles are screened in this geometry, and in a solution with a second scalar, which falls off as $e^{-3r/L}$ near the boundary, that scalar is the gaugino condensate of the field theory [girardello2000]. Freedman, Gubser, Pilch, and Warner solved flows of another kind in closed form, in which scalar expectation values break the gauge symmetry, and whose geometries in ten dimensions are continuous distributions of D3-branes [freedman2000]. For the branes spread over a uniform disc they found a mass gap in a correlator of two operators and "perfect screening" of quarks [freedman2000].¶Jan de Boer, Erik Verlinde, and Herman Verlinde wrote the equations of supergravity along $r$ as a problem of Hamilton and Jacobi in 2000, and found that the action on the boundary obeys the Callan-Symanzik equations [deboer2000]. Pilch and Warner lifted the wall of Freedman and coauthors to ten dimensions in full, and found that the flow of Girardello and coauthors becomes in ten dimensions a dielectric 7-brane in the infrared, with a singularity that they interpreted as a ring of 5-branes [pilch2000]. Steven S. Gubser proposed in 2000 that these walls may have large curvatures only where the scalar potential stays bounded above, as in the flow of Girardello and coauthors [gubser2000]. Massimo Bianchi, Freedman, and Skenderis renormalised the action of supergravity on the flow of Girardello and coauthors and on the disc of branes in 2001, and computed correlators of two stress tensors [bianchi2001]. On the disc, where conformal symmetry breaks spontaneously, those correlators have a pole at zero mass, and in the flow of Girardello and coauthors, where a mass breaks it explicitly, they have none [bianchi2001].¶Robert C. Myers and Aninda Sinha added terms of second and third order in the curvature to gravity in 2010, so that the two central charges $a$ and $c$ of the field theory in four dimensions differ, and found that the flow of $a$ is monotonic and the flow of $c$ is not [myers2010seeing]. Extending the analysis to other dimensions, they conjectured a $c$-theorem in arbitrary dimensions for a coefficient $a^*_d$ in the entanglement entropy between two halves of a sphere [myers2010seeing]. Evan Deddo, James T. Liu, Leopoldo A. Pando Zayas, and Robert J. Saskowski reproved the $c$-, $F$-, and $a$-theorems in two, three, and four dimensions in 2024 from the null energy condition and the Ryu-Takayanagi formula, starting from the inequality of Freedman and coauthors [deddo2024, freedman1999].

related.text: Near its boundary each flow here approaches anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions, the conformal vacuum of $\mathcal{N} = 4$ super Yang-Mills theory. The inner end of Freedman and coauthors' wall is anti-de Sitter space again, with a smaller radius [freedman1999].

The throat of coincident three-branes, anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions times a sphere, where every flow here starts. Spread over a uniform disc, the branes give the flow of the Coulomb branch solved in closed form [freedman2000].

Two walls of zero thickness in anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions. DeWolfe, Freedman, Gubser, and Karch held them apart with a scalar in the bulk, solving the equations of first order of these flows in closed form [dewolfe2000].

A thin wall with flat space on either side. Walls between regions of anti-de Sitter space with different radii had been studied in supergravity of four dimensions before the flows here, in five [skenderis1999].

A wall of five dimensional gauged supergravity from M-theory, with the volume of a Calabi-Yau space as its scalar, falling toward one of the two walls that end the fifth dimension [lukas1999universe].

coordinates.name: Confining Flow, Proper Distance

parameters.description: Radius of the anti-de Sitter space the flow approaches at its boundary, a length

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x_1, x_2, x_3, r)$, with $t$ having dimensions of time, $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ lengths along the wall, and $r$ the proper distance from the singularity, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $\lambda$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Confining Flow, Coordinate $u$

parameters.description: Radius of the anti-de Sitter space the flow approaches at its boundary, a length

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x_1, x_2, x_3, u)$, with $t$ having dimensions of time and $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ lengths along the wall, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The coordinate $u = 1 - e^{-2r/L}$ is that of Bianchi, Freedman, and Skenderis [bianchi2001], where $r$ is the proper distance from the singularity. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $\lambda$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = \dfrac{u}{1 - u}\left(-c^2dt^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2\right) + \dfrac{L^2\,du^2}{4\left(1 - u\right)^2}

coordinates.name: Coulomb Branch Disc

parameters.description: Radius of the anti-de Sitter space the flow approaches at its boundary, a length
Radius of the disc of D3-branes in ten dimensions, a length

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x_1, x_2, x_3, v)$, with $t$ having dimensions of time and $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ lengths along the wall, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The coordinate $v = e^{\sqrt{6}\Phi}$ is that of Bianchi, Freedman, and Skenderis [bianchi2001], with $\Phi$ the scalar of the flow. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $\lambda$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = \dfrac{\ell^2v^{2/3}}{L^2\left(1 - v\right)}\left(-c^2dt^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2\right) + \dfrac{L^2\,dv^2}{4v^{4/3}\left(1 - v\right)^2}
